objects.original: A finite Euclidean process whose rows are continuous finite-variation processes plus completed coordinate Itô integrals; compact range K with fallback, and a C² scalar test.
objects.reconstructed: Finite state type I and Brownian type J; eta_ij; finite-variation coordinate processes A_i; resulting X; compact K and fallback∈K; scalar f. Second-order Taylor remainder R_f.

domains.original: Finite state coordinates I and finite Brownian coordinates J (DecidableEq J); finite sample measure and nonnegative-time filtration; fixed T>0; K is a compact subset of ℝ^I with a selected point.
domains.reconstructed: Omega is measurable with finite measure mu and a filtration F indexed by nonnegative reals. T>0 is fixed. The Euclidean coordinate type J is finite with decidable equality. B:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^J. lambda_T denotes the pullback under NNReal.toReal of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T]. I is finite. No DecidableEq I argument is required. A_i:[0,infinity)×Omega→R; X:[0,infinity)×Omega→R^I; f:R^I→R; K⊆R^I.

assumptions.original: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure. The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable. The drift paths are almost surely continuous and have bounded variation on [0,T]. The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of that range.
assumptions.reconstructed: Assumptions: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). For every i and t≤T, A_i(t,·) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For every i, mu-a.e. omega, A_i(·,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T]. K compact, fallback∈K; f is ambient C² at every point of K. On one mu-full set, X(t,omega)∈K for every t≤T. No progressivity of A_i is explicitly assumed.

conclusion.original: For the completed Euclidean Itô process staying in a compact K throughout the horizon almost surely, and a scalar test twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at every point of K, the sum of second-order Taylor residuals along its dyadic increments converges in measure to zero. Formula: \sum_i\left(f(X_{t_{i+1}})-f(X_{t_i})-Df(X_{t_i})[\Delta_iX]-\tfrac12D^2f(X_{t_i})[\Delta_iX,\Delta_iX]\right)\xrightarrow{\mu}0.
conclusion.reconstructed: Conclusion: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Define X_i(t)=A_i(t)+∑_j I_j(eta_ij)(t), t_r^n=rT/2^n, Delta_r^n X=X(t_{r+1}^n)-X(t_r^n). With R_f(x,v)=f(x+v)-f(x)-Df(x)[v]-(1/2)D²f(x)[v,v], the functions ∑_{r=0}^{2^n-1}R_f(X(t_r^n),Delta_r^n X) converge in mu-measure to zero.

quantifiers.original: For all data satisfying the listed assumptions and one a.e. event of confinement for every t≤T, the actual-increment residual sums converge in measure.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Quantifier order: Universally quantify setup, A, compact K, fallback and f. Under the full-measure all-time range condition X(t,omega)∈K for t≤T, the stated dyadic sums converge in measure.

scopes.original: Fixed positive horizon and in-measure limit only. Drift marginal measurability is separately at each fixed time; continuity, bounded variation and confinement are a.e. path properties. Drift progressivity is not required.
scopes.reconstructed: Scope: Fixed positive horizon; dyadic sequence n→infinity; convergence in measure only. A_i need not be given as a drift integral. Path and range hypotheses are almost sure and simultaneous in time, whereas A_i's marginal measurability is for each time.

constant_dependencies.original: No numerical rate or new constant; fallback is supplied and is used only for a representative, disappearing from the limiting assertion.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Constant dependencies: No unspecified numerical constants or convergence rate; fallback is supplied but does not occur in the displayed limit.
